Background Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes and microvesicles, are involved in intercellular communication by transferring biomolecules such as mRNA, which has been shown to be as essential biomarkers for many physiological and pathological conditions such as diabetic nephropathy (DN). This study aimed to investigate the expression of CDH1, CDH2, MCP-1, and PAI-1 mRNAs in blood EVs of DN patients and to determine their accuracy in predicting early-stage DN. Methods We recruited 196 participants, including 35 overt DN patients, 53 incipient DN patients, 62 diabetic patients (DM), and 46 healthy individuals. Quantification of the mRNA profile of blood EVs was performed using the qRT-PCR method. The diagnostic performance of mRNA was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results The mRNA expression of CDH2 and MCP-1 was downregulated in overt DN group (0.22-fold change and 0.15-fold change, respectively) and incipient DN group (0.60-fold change and 0.43-fold change, respectively) compared to DM group (1.72-fold change and 2.77-fold change, respectively), while PAI-1 mRNA expression decreased in incipient DN group (0.70-fold change) and DM group (0.58-fold change) compared to control. However, the expression level of CDH1 mRNA was not significantly different among the four groups ( p = 0.408). Moreover, CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNAs inversely correlated with creatinine (r = -0.370 and r = -0.361, p <0.001) and Alb/Cr ratio (r = -0.355 and r = -0.297, p <0.001). 1/CDH2 mRNA also predicted overt DN with an accuracy of 0.75 (95%CI: 0.65–0.85) and incipient DN with an accuracy of 0.61 (95%CI: 0.50–0.71) while 1/MCP-1 mRNA had an accuracy of 0.66 (95%CI: 0.55–0.77) for overt DN prediction and an accuracy of 0.61 (95%CI: 0.51–0.71) for incipient DN prediction. Conclusion CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNAs expression in blood EVs was decreased with the development of DN, suggesting the renoprotective effect of these mRNAs in diabetic individuals. Moreover, their quantifications could serve as diagnostic biomarkers for early-stage DN. The authors received no specific funding for this work. extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the diagnostic potential of CDH1, CDH2, MCP-1, and PAI-1 mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles (EVs) for predicting early-stage diabetic nephropathy (DN) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The main findings indicate that CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression in blood EVs was significantly downregulated with the development of DN (overt and incipient stages) compared to diabetic patients without DN, suggesting a renoprotective effect and their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. These mRNAs inversely correlated with markers of kidney damage like creatinine and albuminuria. In contrast, CDH1 mRNA showed no significant change across groups, and while PAI-1 mRNA decreased in some diabetic groups, its diagnostic utility for early DN was not clearly established, according to the authors' results. The study also explored the expression of these and other related biomarkers in urine.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 196 participants (35 overt DN, 53 incipient DN, 62 DM, and 46 healthy controls) with type 2 diabetes. The study focused on characterizing mRNA expression levels in blood extracellular vesicles and other clinical markers across different stages of diabetic nephropathy and healthy controls. No therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were administered or reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated in overt DN group (0.22-fold change relative to DM group, more downregulated than incipient DN, p < 0.001) and incipient DN group (0.60-fold change relative to DM group, p = 0.042). Expressed less in overt DN group than incipient DN (p = 0.013), DM (p < 0.001), and control (p < 0.001). Inversely correlated with HbA1c (r = -0.183, p = 0.012), urea (r = -0.152, p = 0.035), creatinine (r = -0.370, p < 0.001), and urine Alb/Cr ratio (r = -0.355, p < 0.001). 1/CDH2 mRNA predicted overt DN with an accuracy of 0.75 (95%CI: 0.65–0.85, AUC 0.75) and incipient DN with an accuracy of 0.61 (95%CI: 0.50–0.71, AUC 0.61, sensitivity 37.7%, specificity 83.9% at cutoff 3.47). Optimal diagnostic performance for overt DN at 2.14-fold change (sensitivity 74.3%, specificity 69.4%).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cadherin-2 (N-cadherin) is involved in cell-cell adhesion and is suggested to have a renoprotective effect in diabetic individuals. Its downregulation correlates with impaired kidney function and is associated with renal fibrosis detection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diabetic Nephropathy progression (overt DN, incipient DN) and Diabetic Mellitus patients, compared to healthy controls. Relevant for early-stage DN development and monitoring.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased expression suggests a renoprotective effect and serves as a diagnostic biomarker for early-stage DN, with its inverse correlation to kidney damage markers (creatinine, albuminuria). Useful for detecting early-stage DN, stratifying patients, and monitoring therapy response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated in overt DN group (0.15-fold change relative to DM group) and incipient DN group (0.43-fold change relative to DM group). Overt DN group had lower level than DM and control (p = 0.002 for both). Incipient DN group expressed less compared to DM (p = 0.008) and control (p = 0.001). Negatively correlated with creatinine (r = -0.361, p < 0.001) and urine Alb/Cr ratio (r = -0.297, p < 0.001). 1/MCP-1 mRNA predicted overt DN with an accuracy of 0.66 (95%CI: 0.55–0.77, AUC 0.66) and incipient DN with an accuracy of 0.61 (95%CI: 0.51–0.71, AUC 0.61, sensitivity 69.8%, specificity 61.3% at cutoff 0.61).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Monocyte Chemoattractant Protein-1 (MCP-1) is a chemokine regulating monocyte/macrophage trafficking in inflammation. Its decrease in this context is suggested to have a renoprotective effect in diabetic individuals and is associated with renal fibrosis detection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diabetic Nephropathy progression (overt DN, incipient DN) and Diabetic Mellitus patients, compared to healthy controls. Relevant for early-stage DN development and monitoring.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased expression suggests a renoprotective effect and serves as a diagnostic biomarker for early-stage DN, with its inverse correlation to kidney damage markers (creatinine, albuminuria). Useful for detecting early-stage DN, stratifying patients, and monitoring therapy response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased in incipient DN group (0.70-fold change) and DM group (0.58-fold change) compared to control. However, authors' results did not indicate a strong role in early detection of DN.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 (SERPINE1) plays a role in fibrinolysis, blood clotting, cell motility, and adhesion, with implications in fibrosis relevant to renal pathology.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Incipient diabetic nephropathy and diabetic patients (DM) compared to healthy controls; early-stage diabetic nephropathy prediction.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Observed decrease in expression is associated with incipient diabetic nephropathy and the diabetic state. While potentially a predictor of renal fibrosis, its diagnostic utility for early-stage DN in this study was not significant.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression level was not significantly different among the four groups (p = 0.408). Kruskal–Wallis analyses showed no significant difference in expression fold change between four study groups. Authors' results did not indicate a role in early detection of DN.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cadherin-1 (E-cadherin) is a cell-cell adhesion molecule crucial for maintaining epithelial integrity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diabetic nephropathy (Overt DN, Incipient DN, DM) and healthy individuals; early-stage diabetic nephropathy prediction.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Not a significant indicator for early-stage diabetic nephropathy based on this study's findings due to lack of significant change in expression. No significant diagnostic potential found in blood EVs.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overt DN group and incipient DN group had higher urine Alb/Cr ratio than the DM group and control (p < 0.001). Inversely correlated with CDH2 mRNA (r = -0.355, p < 0.001) and MCP-1 mRNA (r = -0.297, p < 0.001).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney damage and albuminuria, reflecting impaired kidney function and glomerular filtration barrier integrity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diabetic Nephropathy progression (incipient DN and overt DN) compared to Diabetic Mellitus (DM) and control groups.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are indicative of Diabetic Nephropathy progression and kidney dysfunction. Severity of kidney damage, a key diagnostic criterion for DN, inversely correlated with potential renoprotective markers.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CDH2 mRNA level inversely correlated with HbA1c (Spearman correlation coefficient = -0.183, p = 0.012).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of long-term blood glucose control.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlation with CDH2 mRNA levels suggests an association with DN progression.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CDH2 mRNA level inversely correlated with urea (Spearman correlation coefficient = -0.152, p = 0.035). CDH2 mRNA expression level could be estimated from urea (unstandardized coefficient = 0.035, p = 0.019).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney function, specifically nitrogenous waste product clearance.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Correlated with CDH2 mRNA levels, suggesting an association with kidney function in DN.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CDH2 mRNA level inversely correlated with creatinine (Spearman correlation coefficient = -0.370, p < 0.001). MCP-1 mRNA had negative correlations with creatinine (Spearman correlation coefficient = -0.361, p < 0.001). Incipient DN group had higher concentration than DM group (p = 0.001), but no significant difference compared to control (p = 0.151). CDH2 mRNA expression level could be estimated from creatinine (unstandardized coefficient = -2.673, p < 0.001). MCP-1 mRNA expression level could be estimated from creatinine level (unstandardized coefficient = -3.024, p = 0.010).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of kidney function. Elevated levels suggest impaired kidney function, and are inversely correlated with potential renoprotective markers.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Inversely correlated with CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA levels, reflecting kidney function and severity of renal injury. Acts as a predictor of CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant correlation between eGFR and CDH2 and MCP-1 mRNA expression was found. Four study groups had no significant difference in eGFR, and all participants had normal eGFR despite different degrees of albuminuria.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Normal eGFR indicated early stages of Diabetic Nephropathy in participants, despite varying levels of albuminuria. Not found to correlate with CDH2 or MCP-1 mRNA expression in this study's context.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Inversely associated with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR); predicts DN with an accuracy of 0.705.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Associated with glomeruli damage and renal function.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates glomeruli damage and early renal failure; predicts DN with 0.705 accuracy.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in DN patients compared with healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Produces E-cadherin, a calcium-dependent adhesion protein fundamental in intercellular adhesion.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Abnormal expression causes diseases such as DN, diabetic retinopathy, and epithelial-derived solid tumors. Acts as a potential predictor of renal fibrosis due to chronic kidney disease, obstructive nephropathy, and DN.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 15-fold higher in DN patients compared with healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Produces N-cadherin, a calcium-dependent adhesion protein fundamental in intercellular adhesion.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Abnormal expression causes diseases such as DN, diabetic retinopathy, and epithelial-derived solid tumors. Acts as a potential predictor of renal fibrosis due to chronic kidney disease, obstructive nephropathy, and DN.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in DN patients compared with healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Produces chemokines that play a pivotal role in regulating monocyte/macrophage trafficking in the inflammatory process.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Abnormal expression leads to DN, diabetic retinopathy, insulin resistance, atherosclerosis, and other inflammatory conditions. Acts as a potential predictor of renal fibrosis due to chronic kidney disease, obstructive nephropathy, and DN.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in DN patients compared with healthy controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Produces plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (SERPINE1), playing a major role in hemostasis by inhibiting plasminogen activators mediated fibrinolysis and in cell motility and adhesion.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Abnormal gene expression leads to various diseases such as DN and cardiovascular disease due to DM. Acts as a potential predictor of renal fibrosis due to chronic kidney disease, obstructive nephropathy, and DN.
